supporting_observations.claim: Two network logon attempts for noah.kim failed with an incorrect-password status (SubStatus 0xc000006a) at 13:44 and 13:45 UTC; both identify 198.51.100.201 as the source.

At 13:46 UTC, a network logon for noah.kim succeeded and records the same source IP, 198.51.100.201, as the preceding failures. The failed attempts followed by success from that address support treating this as a potentially successful unauthorized authentication.

The recorded authentication is a network logon (LogonType 3), not evidence of an interactive logon at WS-NKIM-01. The successful event records DC-MAP-01 as WorkstationName while retaining 198.51.100.201 as IpAddress.

known_telemetry_limitations: The records do not identify who or what controlled source IP 198.51.100.201, or map it to a known host.
The evidence contains two failed attempts and one success; it does not establish a larger volume of attempts.
The available records do not show the source-side process, the cause of the successful authentication, or activity performed using the successful logon.
claims_not_established: That noah.kim's credentials were compromised or that the account owner initiated or approved these logons.
That the source address was outside the organization's network or definitively unauthorized; the supplied records do not map the address to an owner or location.
That the successful logon led to access to data or further malicious activity.
additional_evidence_needed: Correlate 198.51.100.201 with network address assignments, firewall, NAT, and perimeter logs at the event times.
Collect domain controller authentication and session records around 13:44–13:46 UTC to identify the resulting session and any subsequent access.
Check whether the source address or this authentication pattern appears in other account and host logs, and verify with noah.kim whether the activity was expected.
